hep_tracking.benchmark module

Benchmarking utilities for Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) models.

class hep_tracking.benchmark.ANNBenchmarkRunner(k_neighbors: int = 5, warmup_runs: int = 1, num_runs: int = 3)[source]

Bases: object

Runner for evaluating nearest neighbor search models against datasets.

This class manages the lifecycle of benchmarking, including warmup iterations, timed query runs, recall calculation, and explicit memory management to prevent OOM (Out Of Memory) errors during sequential evaluations.

k_neighbors

Number of nearest neighbors to retrieve during queries.

warmup_runs

Number of un-timed query executions to run before benchmarking.

num_runs

Number of timed query executions used to determine minimum query time.

run(models_configs: Sequence[KNNModelConfig], datasets: dict[str, TrackDataset], ground_truth: dict[str, ndarray]) → DataFrame[source]

Execute the benchmark suite on the provided models and datasets.

Iterates through the provided datasets and evaluates each model configuration. For each combination, it measures model build time, executes warmup runs, measures query times over multiple runs, and calculates Queries Per Second (QPS) and recall. Memory is explicitly collected between model evaluations, including CuPy memory pools if available, to ensure clean runs.

Parameters:

  • models_configs – A sequence of configuration objects defining the models to instantiate and benchmark.

  • datasets – A dictionary mapping dataset names to dataset instances.

  • ground_truth – A dictionary mapping dataset names to their corresponding ground truth index arrays.

Returns:

A pandas DataFrame containing performance metrics (Build_Time_s, Query_Time_s, QPS, Recall) for every tested model and dataset combination.

hep_tracking.classifiers.evaluate_classifier_throughput(model, test_dataset: TrackDataset, batch_sizes: tuple[int, ...] = (1, 1000, 10000), num_runs: int = 5) → dict[int, float][source]

Measure the inference throughput of a model across different batch sizes.

Executes a warm-up prediction and then measures performance over several iterations to capture the optimal operational speed per batch size.

Parameters:

  • model – A trained classifier instance implementing predict_proba.

  • test_dataset – The dataset object containing testing features (X).

  • batch_sizes – A tuple of integers representing the number of samples to process in a single batch. Defaults to (1, 1000, 10000).

  • num_runs – The number of measured timing runs to perform for each batch size. Defaults to 5.

Returns:

A dictionary mapping the batch size integer to its calculated throughput in items processed per second.

hep_tracking.classifiers.optimize_hyperparameters(estimator, param_distributions: dict, train_dataset: TrackDataset, val_dataset: TrackDataset, n_iter: int = 10, random_state: int = 42) → dict[source]

Perform a randomized hyperparameter search across a predefined validation split.

This function securely splits the data by passing an explicit fold array to PredefinedSplit. This ensures that RandomizedSearchCV evaluates solely on the provided validation dataset without mixing test sets.

Parameters:

  • estimator – An uninitialized classifier object conforming to the scikit-learn API.

  • param_distributions – Dictionary containing parameter names (strings) as keys and lists of parameters or distributions to sample from as values.

  • train_dataset – The primary dataset used for fitting the model.

  • val_dataset – The holdout dataset used exclusively for scoring each configuration.

  • n_iter – The number of parameter settings that are sampled. Defaults to 10.

  • random_state – The seed used for reproducible random sampling. Defaults to 42.

Returns:

A dictionary containing the parameter settings that yielded the best ROC-AUC score on the validation set.

hep_tracking.data module

Synthetic data generation for high-energy physics tracking datasets.

This module provides functions to simulate particle trajectories, generate background noise, and package these into complete datasets saved as compressed numpy arrays.

hep_tracking.data.generate_datasets(configs: list[DatasetConfig], output_dir: str = 'data') → None[source]

Generate and serialize multiple synthetic datasets based on configurations.

Iterates through the provided dataset configurations, calculating the required number of events and hits per event. It aggregates the generated features, labels, and event IDs, then saves them as compressed .npz archives to the specified output directory. Track IDs are offset globally across events to ensure uniqueness within a single dataset.

Parameters:

  • configs – A list of configurations detailing the size and simulation parameters for each target dataset.

  • output_dir – The target directory path where the .npz files will be saved. The directory is created if it does not exist. Defaults to “data”.

hep_tracking.data.generate_tracks(n_tracks: int, n_noise: int, config: TrackSimulationConfig, seed_offset: int = 0) → tuple[ndarray, ndarray][source]

Generate synthetic particle tracks and noise hits for a single event.

Simulates linear particle trajectories originating near the origin (vertex) and propagating outwards. Adds Gaussian noise to the positions and directional vectors, and uniformly distributes random noise hits throughout the volume. The returned arrays are randomly permuted so the sequence of hits does not trivially reveal the underlying tracks.

Parameters:

  • n_tracks – The number of distinct particle tracks to simulate.

  • n_noise – The total number of uncorrelated noise hits to inject.

  • config – The simulation parameters controlling geometry and variance.

  • seed_offset – An integer added to the base configuration seed to ensure uncorrelated randomness across different events. Defaults to 0.

Returns:

  • features: A (N, 5) array of hit features representing position and direction.

  • labels: A (N,) array of track IDs, where -1 indicates a noise hit.

Return type:

A tuple containing two arrays

hep_tracking.features module

Feature engineering and dataset manipulation for hit pairs.

hep_tracking.features.compute_pair_features(features_a: ndarray, features_b: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Compute relative geometric features between pairs of track hits.

Calculates a 7-dimensional feature vector for each pair, encompassing spatial differences, cylindrical radius differences, angular relationships, and vector dot products.

Parameters:

  • features_a – Feature matrix of the query hits.

  • features_b – Feature matrix of the candidate neighbor hits.

Returns:

A (N, 7) float32 array containing the computed pairwise features.

hep_tracking.features.create_pair_dataset(dataset: TrackDataset, candidate_indices: ndarray, max_neg_ratio: float = 5.0, seed: int = 42) → TrackDataset[source]

Construct a dataset of hit pairs for binary classification.

Transforms nearest-neighbor candidate indices into a binary classification dataset. Pairs belonging to the same track are labeled as positive (1), while mismatched hits or noise hits are labeled as negative (0). To address class imbalance, the negative class is randomly downsampled.

Parameters:

  • dataset – The source track dataset containing original features and labels.

  • candidate_indices – An array of shape (N, K) representing the nearest neighbor indices for each hit.

  • max_neg_ratio – Maximum allowable ratio of negative to positive pairs. Defaults to 5.0.

  • seed – Random seed used for shuffling and downsampling. Defaults to 42.

Returns:

A new TrackDataset object where X contains the pairwise features and y contains binary classification labels.

hep_tracking.features.split_by_event(dataset: TrackDataset, train_size: float = 0.75, val_size: float = 0.15, seed: int = 42) → tuple[TrackDataset, TrackDataset, TrackDataset][source]

Split a dataset into training, validation, and test sets by event.

Groups data strictly by event_ids to ensure there is no data leakage across splits. Hits belonging to the same event will always remain together in the same dataset partition.

Parameters:

  • dataset – The source dataset to be split.

  • train_size – The proportion of unique events allocated to the training set. Defaults to 0.75.

  • val_size – The proportion of unique events allocated to the validation set. Defaults to 0.15.

  • seed – Random seed used to shuffle the unique events prior to splitting. Defaults to 42.

Returns:

the training set, the validation set, and the test set.

Return type:

A tuple containing three TrackDataset instances

Raises:

ValueError – If the dataset contains fewer than 3 unique events, making a 3-way split impossible.

hep_tracking.generate_candidates module

Candidate generation utility for track building.

This script processes existing dataset files and generates nearest-neighbor candidates for each hit using an exact KD-Tree search. The results are saved as compressed numpy archives for downstream pair classification.

hep_tracking.generate_candidates.generate_and_save_candidates(data_dir: str = 'data', k_neighbors: int = 5, spatial_only: bool = False)[source]

Generate and save nearest-neighbor candidate pairs for datasets in a directory.

Scans the specified directory for .npz files matching the dataset_*.npz pattern. For each distinct event within a dataset, it computes the exact K-nearest neighbors using a KD-Tree. The resulting global candidate indices and their corresponding distances are saved to a new .npz file with a candidates_ prefix.

Parameters:

  • data_dir – Directory containing the input dataset files. The output candidate files will also be saved here. Defaults to “data”.

  • k_neighbors – The number of nearest neighbors to retrieve for each hit. Defaults to 5.

  • spatial_only – If True, distance calculations rely strictly on the first three geometric features (typically x, y, z). If False, all available features are used. Defaults to False.

hep_tracking.models module

Wrappers for exact and approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search algorithms.

This module provides a unified interface for evaluating various nearest neighbor implementations, including brute-force matrix operations (NumPy/CuPy), tree-based methods (SciPy/Scikit-learn), and highly optimized ANN libraries (FAISS/HNSWlib).

hep_tracking.models.filter_gpu_configs(configs: list, verbose: bool = True) → list[source]

Drop model configs that explicitly require GPU (use_gpu=True) if none is available.

Intended for notebooks/cells whose whole point is an intentional CPU vs GPU comparison (e.g. crossover-N experiments), where use_gpu=True configs are deliberate and must NOT be silently downgraded to CPU (that would make the comparison meaningless). On a machine without a working GPU, this instead removes those specific configs up-front (with a clear message) so the rest of the notebook still runs to completion on whatever CPU-only configs remain, rather than crashing deep inside the benchmark loop.

Parameters:

  • configs – A list of KNNModelConfig (or similar) objects, each with a .model_kwargs dict that may contain a use_gpu key.

  • verbose – If True, prints which configs (if any) were skipped.

Returns:

A new list with any use_gpu=True configs removed if no GPU is available; otherwise the original list unchanged.

hep_tracking.models.is_gpu_available() → bool[source]

Check whether a working FAISS GPU backend is available on this machine.

The result is cached after the first call, since the underlying check (allocating GPU resources) is relatively expensive and the answer cannot change during the lifetime of the process.

Returns:

True if at least one CUDA GPU is visible to FAISS, False otherwise (e.g. no GPU present, no CUDA driver, or a CPU-only faiss-cpu install with no GPU support compiled in).

hep_tracking.pipeline module

Pipeline evaluation strategies for high-energy physics track building.

class hep_tracking.pipeline.PipelineEvaluator(dataset: TrackDataset, k_neighbors: int, geom_cuts: dict, ml_threshold: float = 0.5, warmup_runs: int = 0, num_runs: int = 1)[source]

Bases: object

Evaluates different candidate generation and filtering pipelines.

This class provides standardized methods for running and timing various track-building pipelines (e.g., geometric cuts, machine learning, and brute-force). It automatically calculates the theoretical maximum number of valid pairs in the dataset to establish baseline efficiency.

dataset

The dataset containing hit features and ground truth labels.

k_neighbors

The number of nearest neighbors to retrieve during the candidate generation phase.

geom_cuts

Dictionary containing threshold values for geometric filtering (e.g., ‘max_delta_r’, ‘min_dot_product’).

ml_threshold

Probability cutoff for the machine learning classifier.

true_pairs_count

Precalculated total number of valid signal pairs possible within the dataset.

run_all_pairs_pipeline(classifier) → dict[source]

Execute and evaluate a brute-force pipeline comparing all possible hit pairs.

Generates an O(N^2) pairwise grid across the entire dataset before applying the classifier. This is primarily used as a robust baseline or for very small datasets where index creation overhead outweighs the benefit.

Parameters:

classifier – A trained machine learning model implementing predict_proba.

Returns:

A dictionary containing timing breakdowns and final classification metrics.

run_geometric_pipeline(retriever, X_retrieval=None) → dict[source]

Execute and evaluate a pipeline using KNN retrieval and hard geometric cuts.

This method supports precise benchmarking by executing unmeasured warmup iterations followed by multiple measured runs to compute average timings.

Parameters:

  • retriever – An initialized nearest neighbor search object implementing fit and kneighbors.

  • X_retrieval – Optional feature matrix used specifically for the index retrieval step. If None, defaults to self.dataset.X.

Returns:

A dictionary containing averaged timing breakdowns (Time_Retrieval_s, Time_Features_s, Time_Filter_s, Time_Total_s) and performance metrics (Purity, Efficiency, Proposed_Pairs) over the specified number of runs.

run_ml_pipeline(retriever, classifier, X_retrieval=None) → dict[source]

Execute and evaluate a pipeline using KNN retrieval and a machine learning classifier.

This method supports precise benchmarking by executing unmeasured warmup iterations followed by multiple measured runs to compute average timings.

Parameters:

  • retriever – An initialized nearest neighbor search object implementing fit and kneighbors.

  • classifier – A trained machine learning model implementing predict_proba.

  • X_retrieval – Optional feature matrix used specifically for the index retrieval step. If None, defaults to self.dataset.X.

Returns:

A dictionary containing averaged timing breakdowns (Time_Retrieval_s, Time_Features_s, Time_Filter_s, Time_Total_s) and final classification metrics over the specified number of runs.

hep_tracking.plots.plot_3d_hits(dataset: TrackDataset, output_path: str = None)[source]

Plot a 3D scatter visualization of synthetic detector hits.

Distinguishes visually between valid signal tracks (colored by track ID) and background noise (rendered as semi-transparent light gray points).

Parameters:

  • dataset – The dataset containing spatial hit features and track labels.

  • output_path – Optional file path to save the generated figure. If None, the plot is displayed interactively via plt.show().

hep_tracking.plots.plot_distance_distributions(dataset: TrackDataset, output_path: str = None, sample_size: int = 2000)[source]

Plot the pairwise Euclidean distance distributions between hits.

Generates overlapping histograms comparing the distances between hits belonging to the same track versus hits belonging to different tracks. To ensure memory efficiency, the distance matrix is computed on a random subset of the data.

Parameters:

  • dataset – The dataset containing hit features and track labels.

  • output_path – Optional file path to save the generated figure.

  • sample_size – Maximum number of signal hits to sample for the pairwise distance calculation. Defaults to 2000.

hep_tracking.plots.plot_metric_dimension_heatmap(df: DataFrame, metric: str, title: str, cmap: str = 'viridis', log_scale: bool = False, output_path: str = None)[source]

Plot a heatmap of a specific metric across different dataset dimensions and sizes.

Creates subplots for each model found in the DataFrame. The rows correspond to dataset dimensions (‘Dimension’ column) and the columns correspond to dataset sizes (‘Size’ column).

Parameters:

  • df – DataFrame containing at least ‘Model’, ‘Dimension’, ‘Size’, and the target metric column.

  • metric – The column name of the metric to plot (e.g., ‘QPS’ or ‘Recall’).

  • title – The overarching title for the entire figure.

  • cmap – The colormap to use for the heatmap. Defaults to “viridis”.

  • log_scale – If True, applies logarithmic color scaling via LogNorm. Defaults to False.

  • output_path – Optional file path to save the generated figure.

  • title – The overarching title for the entire figure.

hep_tracking.utils module

Evaluation metrics and threshold optimization utilities for classification.

hep_tracking.utils.calculate_classification_metrics(y_true: ndarray, y_pred_proba: ndarray, threshold: float = 0.5) → dict[source]

Calculate a comprehensive suite of binary classification metrics.

Evaluates both continuous probability metrics (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC) and discrete binary metrics (F1, Precision, Recall, Accuracy) by converting the probabilities using the provided threshold.

Parameters:

  • y_true – Ground truth binary labels.

  • y_pred_proba – Predicted probabilities for the positive class.

  • threshold – Probability threshold used to convert continuous probabilities into discrete binary predictions. Defaults to 0.5.

Returns:

A dictionary containing the calculated scores for ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, F1-Score, Precision, Recall, and Accuracy.

hep_tracking.utils.find_best_f1_threshold(y_true: ndarray, y_pred_proba: ndarray) → tuple[float, float][source]

Determine the optimal probability threshold that maximizes the F1 score.

Computes the precision-recall curve and iterates over the generated thresholds to find the exact probability cutoff that yields the highest F1 score for the given dataset. Divides safely by zero where precision and recall are both zero.

Parameters:

  • y_true – Ground truth binary labels.

  • y_pred_proba – Predicted probabilities for the positive class.

Returns:

  • The optimal probability threshold.

  • The corresponding maximum F1 score achieved at that threshold.

Return type:

A tuple containing two floats
